member.summary: Declares that an implementation handles inbound requests for a specific channelId. Annotated adapters are auto-registered in the so that shared-endpoint (Tier 2) dispatch and SDK features (proactive messaging, diagnostics) can resolve the correct adapter by channelId.

remarks.para: This attribute operates like Microsoft.Agents.Core.Serialization.ActivityTypeAttribute: a source generator (ChannelAdapterInitSourceGenerator) emits an assembly-level for every annotated adapter, and those assembly attributes are read off the loaded assemblies at runtime — so no explicit DI registration call (such as AddChannelAdapter) is required. Simply reference the assembly that declares the annotated adapter.

The annotated type must implement (so it can be resolved through ) and should be public so consuming applications can preload its assembly; to also serve shared-endpoint HTTP dispatch it must implement the host's HTTP adapter contract (IAgentHttpAdapter in Microsoft.Agents.Hosting.AspNetCore). CloudAdapter implements both contracts; a type deriving directly from ChannelAdapter must implement the host contract separately when it participates in HTTP dispatch. It does not need to derive from CloudAdapter — the default Activity Protocol adapter (CloudAdapter) remains the registry default and is not annotated.

member.remarks:
A passes incoming activities from the user's channel to the middleware's method.
You can add middleware objects to your adapter’s middleware collection. The adapter processes and directs incoming activities in through the Agent middleware pipeline to your Agent’s logic and then back out again. As each activity flows in and out of the Agent, each piece of middleware can inspect or act upon the activity, both before and after the Agent logic runs.
For each activity, the adapter calls middleware in the order in which you added it.

member.name: T:Microsoft.Agents.Builder.StreamingResponse
member.summary:
This class enables sending chunked text in a series of "intermediate" messages, on an interval. This gives the UX of a streamed message. When complete, a final message (ActivityType.Message) is sent with the full message and optional Attachments.
The expected sequence of calls is:
`QueueInformativeUpdateAsync()`, `QueueTextChunk()`, `QueueTextChunk()`, ..., `EndStreamAsync()`.
Once `EndStreamAsync()` is called, the stream is considered ended and no further updates can be sent.
member.remarks: Only Teams and WebChat support streaming messages. However, channels that do not support streaming messages will only receive the final message when is called.

This class support throttling via the property. Teams and Azure Channels require some throttling since services like OpenAI produce streams that exceed allowed Channel message limits. Teams defaults to 1000ms per intermediate message, and WebChat 500ms. Reducing the Interval could result in message delivery failures.

member.summary: Timer callback that drives the streaming of buffered activities to the client.
member.remarks:
This method is invoked on each timer tick while a stream is active. On every pass it:
Guards against re-entrancy: if a previous callback is still running (), it returns immediately.
Updates based on the time since the stream started.
For the M365 Copilot (BizChat) channel, evaluates two conditions:
Timeout: if the total elapsed time is at or beyond , the stream is considered timed out. Depending on whether any text has been sent, either a timeout message or a space plus terminating block is sent, the timer is stopped, and streaming is disabled so the channel falls back to async (non-streaming) delivery.
Working notice: if more than (~45 seconds) has elapsed since the last pass and the queue is empty, an informative "working" update is queued to keep the BizChat stream alive.
Dequeues and sends the next buffered activity (if any). If the queue is empty and the stream has ended, it signals completion and stops the timer; otherwise it shortens the interval to pick up the next chunk sooner.
Because the timer runs on a background thread, exceptions are handled within rather than propagated, and awaits are performed outside of any lock.

member.name: T:Microsoft.Agents.Builder.UserAuth.TokenService.OAuthFlow
member.summary: Creates a new prompt that asks the user to sign in using the Token Service. service.

remarks.para: The prompt will attempt to retrieve the users current token and if the user isn't signed in, it will send them an `OAuthCard|SigninCard` containing a button they can press to signin. Depending on the channel, the user will be sent through one of two possible signin flows:
- The automatic signin flow where once the user signs in and the SSO service will forward the Agent the users access token using either an `event` or `invoke` activity.

- The "magic code" flow where once the user signs in they will be prompted by the SSO service to send the Agent a six digit code confirming their identity. This code will be sent as a standard `message` activity.
Both flows are automatically supported by the `OAuthFlow` and the only thing you need to be careful of is that you don't block the `event` and `invoke` activities that the prompt might be waiting on.
